title: A Pilot Study to Evaluate the Noci Stim Instrument in Patients With Non-Radiating Low Back Pain
official: A Pilot Study to Evaluate the Noci Stim Instrument in Patients With Non-Radiating Low Back Pain: Assessing Device Parameters, Clinical Endpoints, and Feasibility for a Pivotal Trial (ENABLE)
summary: This is a prospective, single-center, single-operator (Noci Stim) pilot comparative diagnostic study. The study evaluates agreement between expert manual palpation and Noci Stim electrical stimulation for identifying pain-generating muscles in patients with non-radiating low back pain. Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy (MRS) is included as an exploratory modality to investigate biochemical correlates of clinically identified pain-generating muscles. The study is designed to confirm device parameters, assess endpoint robustness, and generate data to support pivotal study design.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults aged 18-75 years at the time of enrollment.
* Presenting with non-radiating low back pain of sufficient duration and severity to warrant clinical evaluation.
* Willing and able to participate in manual palpation assessment, Noci Stim electrical stimulation assessment, and MRS.
* Ability to remain motionless for the duration of the MRS scan (approximately 60 minutes).
* Written informed consent obtained prior to any study-specific procedure.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Radiating leg pain or clinical signs of radiculopathy.
* Back surgery within the preceding 6 months.
* Implanted pacemaker, neurostimulator, or other device contraindicated for electrical stimulation.
* Contraindication to MRI or MRS (e.g., incompatible metallic implants, severe claustrophobia).
* Known contraindication to manual palpation of the study muscles.
* Pregnancy or lactation.
* Co-existing medical or psychiatric condition that, in the judgment of the investigator, could interfere with study assessments or place the subject at undue risk (e.g., active malignancy, active psychosis).
